notes: The effect of this arrow on secondary targets is exactly the same as a regular shot, with the exception of halving the damage source component (weapon damage + weapon enchantment + ability modifier).
The halving has no effect on damage riders (damage bonuses other than listed above). Notable bonuses unaffected by the reduction include Sharpshooter: All In and Titan Weapon of the Titanstring Bow.

Arrows may ricochet:
Off any target, including inanimate objects, which is useful against targets otherwise protected by Sanctuary.
Into neutral characters and Knocked Out enemies.
Into invisible characters and break their Invisibility.
Arrows do not ricochet into Darkness.
There is a bug, such that if the first arrow crits, all subsequent hits will also crit. This can be forced with Hold Person or Hold Monster.

Characters under the effects of an Elixir of Bloodlust can use this arrow to gain an additional action point by targeting the arrow at an object. When the object "dies" and a living creature is then hit by the same effect, the game gives you an additional action for killing an enemy, as per the Elixir. This also works with Chain Lightning.

Drinking multiple Greater Elixirs of Arcane Cultivation in a row will not restore multiple spell slots. However, if you alternate between drinking this and a different elixir, you can restore multiple slots. For example, drinking a Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation, then a Elixir of Arcane Cultivation, and then another Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation will restore two level 2 slots and one level 1 slot.

If drunk by a Warlock, the extra spell slot will behave like a Spellcasting spell slot rather than a Pact Magic spell slot — i.e., it will always be level 2 regardless of the Warlock's level, and it will not be restored by taking a short rest. However, it is still possible to cast Warlock spells with it.

If drunk by a spellcasting character who only has level 1 spell slots at their current level, this elixir will still give them a level 2 spell slot. Although this does not provide access to any level 2 spells, they can still use the extra spell slot to upcast level 1 spells.
If drunk by a character with no spellcasting features at all, this elixir will still give them a single level 2 spell slot, though they will not be able to use it for anything.

bugs:
A Smokepowder Bomb detonates and deals its damage when the bomb itself takes damage, regardless of source or type. Normally, this occurs when the thrown bomb hits something (as Throw attacks damage the thrown object). However, the bomb is triggered multiple times if it takes damage from multiple sources at the same time. This can be achieved by stacking multiple damage rider effects that apply to Throw attacks, such as Lightning Charges or Hunter's Mark. Each such effect causes the bomb to simultaneously explode an additional time. This can be used to devastating effect.
An example log of a Smokepowder Bomb triggered multiple times would be:
Character used Throw on Cave-In.
Smokepowder Bomb was hit for 8Bludgeoning damage.
Smokepowder Bomb was hit for 1Lightning damage.
Character destroyed Smokepowder Bomb.
Smokepowder Bomb received 2Bludgeoning damage from falling.
Smokepowder Bomb received 1Lightning damage from falling.
Character blasted Cave-In for 32Force damage.
Character blasted Cave-In for 0Lightning damage.
Character blasted Cave-In for 37Force damage.
Character blasted Cave-In for 0Lightning damage.
The Smokepowder bomb blasted twice: the first time provoking 32Force damage, and the second time provoking 37Force damage.

Another consequence of the detonation occurring when the bomb itself takes damage is that dragging a bomb out of an inventory and onto a Fire surface (or any other surface that deals damage) causes the bomb to detonate immediately. Because dropping items does not use an action, this can be repeated as many times in the same turn as one has bombs (although some careful positioning or resistances may be required to prevent the character moving the bombs from blowing up).

The Haste Spores condition granted by Haste Spore Grenades is similar to that of the Hastened condition granted by speed potions, but only lasts 1 turn instead of 3, and does not leave users with the Lethargic condition when it expires, possibly increasing the utility of Haste Spore Grenades when Thrown over that of Potions of Speed.
